newsitem.title: UK: BA questions EU analysis of alliance routes.
newsitem.headline: BA questions EU analysis of alliance routes.

text.p: British Airways Plc on Thursday queried a European Commission comment on the theoretical impact on airline competition if its proposed transatlantic alliance with American Airlines AMR. goes ahead.

Earlier the EC, which is investigating all U.S.-European alliances following last June's announcement of the BA and American deal, listed 14 routes between British and U.S. cities on which it said the alliance would "eliminate competition".

Senior BA spokesman Michael Blunt told Reuters that of those routes named the two partners only operate on one -- London Gatwick to Dallas, Texas -- on which there would be no competition as a result of the alliance plan.
For the other 13 named city pairs, either BA or American are already currently the sole operators. Six of these are routes from regional airports outside London.

"On many of these routes other airlines could compete if they chose to, and following the (bilateral inter-government) open skies agreement, on which our alliance depends, any US or UK airline would be able to compete with us on any of these routes," Blunt said. "There are also other routes on which our competitors currently fly, on which they face no direct competition," he added.

Britain's Office of Fair Trading issued a more detailed analysis of the competition issues raised by the proposed alliance last month, and other airlines were invited to comment by the end of last week.
Blunt said that all the main alliances between other European and U.S. operators had some degree of exclusivity on the routes they operated.
"United /Lufthansa /SAS fly on 14 city pairs with no direct competition, Delta /Swissair /Sabena /Austrian on 24 city pairs and NorthWest and KLM are alone on 11," he said.

Looking at bilateral flight services between the U.S. and the other European states where alliances are in place, Blunt said there was also a mixed pattern of competition between such alliance partners and other scheduled airlines. For example, he said that while BA/American would face 11 scheduled rival airlines flying between Britain and the United States, United and Lufthansa had 13 direct competitors on routes to and from Germany, KLM and Northwest had nine scheduled competitors on the Dutch market and Delta/Swissair three.
For the three Scandinavian countries covered by SAS, plus Belgium and Austria the scheduled rivals offering direct links to the U.S. number between none and two, Blunt added.
